source_text: 47.1. ''Sed si parens et genitor animarum, inquitis, deus non est, quo auctore progenitae et qua sunt ratione prolatae?''. - Si infucata vultis audire nec ab aliqua vocis ostentatione deducta, item confitemur nos istud ignorare, nescire scientiamque tantae rei non tantum nostram ducimus infirmitatem fragilitatemque transire, verum etiam potestatum quae in mundo sunt omnium et quae numina se esse opinionibus usurpavere mortalium. 2. Sed quas dei negamus, cuius sint debemus ostendere? Minime istud necessario sequitur. Non enim si negemus muscas scarabeos et cimices, nitedulas curculiones et tineas omnipotentis esse opus regig, sequaciter postulandum a nobis est, ut quis ea fecerit institueritque dicamus: possumus enim nulla cum reprehensione nescire, quis et illis originem dederit, et optinere non esse deo ab superiore prolata tam supervacua, tam vana, tam ad nullas pertinentia rationes, quinimmo aliquando et noxia et necessariis inportantia laesiones.
pass_a_gloss: Objector: if God is not parens/genitor of souls, who made them? We confess ignorance—beyond our and even world-powers' scientia. Denial != duty to name the maker (flies/moths analogy): can hold they are not opus of omnipotens rex without naming an alternate.
pass_b_english: 47.1. "But if God is not the parent and begetter of souls," you say, "by what author were they begotten and by what reason brought forth?" — If you wish to hear it unpainted and not drawn from any show of voice, we likewise confess that we are ignorant of that, do not know it, and judge that knowledge of so great a matter surpasses not only our weakness and fragility but even that of all the powers that are in the world and that have seized for themselves by mortals' opinions the name of divinities. 2. But because we deny they are of God, must we show whose they are? That does not follow of necessity. For if we deny that flies, beetles and bugs, dormice, weevils and moths are the work of the almighty King, it is not to be demanded of us in consequence that we say who made and instituted them: we can without any blame not know who gave them origin too, and still maintain that things so superfluous, so empty, so pertaining to no reasons—nay sometimes even harmful and bringing injuries upon necessities—were not brought forth by God from on high.

lemmas.sense: not necessarily the almighty King's work

lemmas.lat: nescire et optinere non esse deo prolata
lemmas.sense: may not-know maker yet hold not from high God

choices.choose: Deny God as soul-begetter without inventing a maker

notes: Image-likeness: refusing divine soul-parentage does not require naming another author.
